title: Selection rules for pinned and quasipinned occupation numbers with degeneracy
abstract: When the natural occupation numbers of a fermionic state saturate a generalized Pauli constraint, the state obeys a selection rule: only those configurations of natural orbitals that saturate the constraint themselves contribute. Pinning thus singles out an active space. The selection rule was proved for non-degenerate occupation numbers; for degenerate ones it was conjectured, and proved for one saturated constraint under an unverified assumption. Here, it is proved for every generalized Pauli constraint, with no assumption, and also in the spin-adapted setting. The rule can only fail for the ordering constraints $λ_j\geλ_{j+1}$. Several saturated constraints are served by one basis whenever their common zero face contains a non-degenerate point. In practice, occupation numbers are quasipinned rather than pinned, and I show what the rule then becomes.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously proves selection rules governing the occupation numbers of fermionic states when these numbers are constrained by generalized Pauli principles. It extends previous results to handle degeneracy without assumptions and provides quantitative bounds for 'quasipinning' scenarios. This work is vital for developing accurate theoretical descriptions of strongly correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The paper establishes selection rules for occupation numbers when these numbers saturate generalized Pauli constraints in fermionic systems.
main_result: It proves the selection rule for every generalized Pauli constraint, even in the degenerate case, and extends the rule to quasipinned states with quantifiable error bounds.
method: The proof combines algebraic techniques related to moment maps, compactness arguments, and analysis of the polytope defined by occupation numbers.
model_or_system: The system involves fermionic states ($\Psi$) whose properties are characterized by the one-body reduced density matrix ($\gamma\Psi$) and its eigenvalues, the natural occupation numbers ($\lambda_\Psi$). The constraints define a polytope ($\Delta_{d,N}$).
key_observables: Natural occupation numbers ($\lambda_j$), the one-body reduced density matrix ($\gamma\Psi$), and the deviation function $f(\Psi)$ from the constraint manifold.
important_parameters: The degree of degeneracy, the specific generalized Pauli constraint $D$, and the small deviation parameter $f(\Psi)$ for quasipinned states.
main_assumptions: The rule fails for ordering constraints ($\lambda_j \ge \lambda_{j+1}$), and the proof for the general case relies on advanced geometric properties of moment maps.
paper_structure: The paper develops from the known non-degenerate case to the general degenerate case, proving the selection rule for all generalized Pauli constraints, and then analyzing the implications for quasipinned states.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of selection rules in the presence of degeneracy and approximations (quasipinning) is crucial for accurately modeling strongly correlated electron systems where simple mean-field approaches fail.
